title: Inspection evidence and restricted handover
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Identify safety and authorisation decisions associated with inspection evidence and restricted handover.
Explain the applicable risk hierarchy and specialist responsibilities for inspection evidence and restricted handover.
Produce a defensible stop-work, competent-person referral or restricted handover using mock evidence.

instruction.heading: Where this lesson sits
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level work, water-fed pole work and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Work above ground level, or work from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted. It needs written employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the state or territory requires for the equipment used. Safe Work Australia's working-heights page sets the high-risk construction threshold at a fall of more than 2 metres. This lesson is a desk-based drill. It does not give permission to work at height or on a solar system.

instruction.heading: What inspection evidence is
instruction.body: Inspection evidence is the record of what was actually looked at, from where, with what limits, and by whom. A worker who looks at the frontage from the ground can see the lower glazing and the frames within reach or sight, and can record what is visible. That view does not show the condition of an upper pane, a fixing above the head, a seal on the far side of a frame, or the state of a structural element. A record that says every window was checked is therefore false when only the ground-level windows were seen. Write down the viewpoint for each observation, and state what was not seen. An observation from a photograph is an observation of that photograph, and it is not a finding about the building.

instruction.heading: Scope closure and the restricted handover
instruction.body: The handover closes the scope in writing. It sets out four parts kept apart from one another. The first is the completed scope: the elevations and areas that were cleaned or inspected under authorisation, and the method used. The second is the excluded elevations: the parts not done, and the reason, such as the restriction on work above ground level or the absence of authorisation. The third is the unresolved conditions: the defects and unknowns observed, with the viewpoint and the time. The fourth is the specialist recommendations and referrals: the person or trade recommended, the person notified, and the time. The handover also states its limits. It does not certify the glazing, the frames or the structure, and it says that nothing above ground level was checked unless that is shown in the completed scope.

instruction.heading: Claims and certification
instruction.body: A handover must not say that the work is certified, compliant or safe unless the evidence and the authority both support the word. The consumer rules are relevant here. The ACCC states that claims must be accurate and backed by reasonable grounds, that a statement giving a false impression can breach the rules even when each word is literally true, that staying silent can mislead a buyer about something that matters, and that intention does not matter. A statement that all windows are certified safe, made after ground-level observation only, would breach those principles. The correct response is to decline the request in writing, give the reason, and offer the referral instead.

instruction.heading: Quotes, scope changes and written agreement
instruction.body: The accepted quote sets the scope. In Western Australia, a quote becomes a binding contract once accepted, and the tradesperson must get the customer's permission before doing extra work. Work done without permission does not have to be paid for. In the Northern Territory, an accepted offer on fixed terms binds both parties, and the customer does not have to pay for extra work that was not in the quote unless it was approved beforehand. These are state and territory rules, and the rule where you work applies. In practice, any added elevation, any added element or any change to the method must be agreed in writing before it is done, and the handover must show the scope that was actually agreed.

instruction.heading: Hazard and safer-option analysis
instruction.body: The lesson case is a client who asks for an all-windows-certified-safe statement after only ground-level observations. Start with the restriction: the upper glazing was not reached under authorisation, so no competence or condition claim about it is supported. Do not give the statement, and do not sign a form that carries it. The safer option is to hand over the ground-level scope with the excluded elevations listed, and to recommend that a building specialist assesses the upper glazing. Any work above ground level would need a separate written scope, an authorised risk assessment and any required licence, and none of that is assumed by this handover.

instruction.heading: Role boundaries and the stop-work decision
instruction.body: General cleaning training does not sign off rope descent, platform operation, anchor certification, electrical clearance or emergency rescue capability, and a trainee cannot certify a building. The stop-work rule applies whenever the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; when wind, rain, ice or fading light changes the conditions; when exposed wiring, damaged cable or water near electrical equipment is seen or suspected; when a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; when the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or when you are asked to work above ground level without the required licence or authorisation. Stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming.

instruction.heading: Records and communication
instruction.body: Use dated records to show the exact observation, the viewpoint, the source document, the person notified, the time, the restriction applied and the response requested. A verbal summary is not a handover. Send the written handover to the site controller or the client, keep a copy, and record the date it was sent and to whom. If the client disagrees with the excluded elevations, record the disagreement and the response, and do not change the handover to match the request without written agreement and evidence.

instruction.heading: Licence notes
instruction.body: A boom-type elevating work platform needs a WP high risk work licence where its boom is 11 metres or more in New South Wales, Western Australia, Tasmania and the Northern Territory. In Queensland, a shorter boom may not need it, because the Queensland definition does not cover platforms shorter than 11 metres. The Victorian WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. The national model code uses the 11-metre threshold, measured from the original design. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria, and the Northern Territory requires the operator to be competent. Completing this lesson is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In NSW, electrical wiring work includes repairing and altering an installation and needs a licence or certificate. Victorian PV rules could not be read in this pass. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

instruction.heading: Trainer-led tabletop practice
instruction.body: Draft a fictional handover note using fictitious work orders, a drawn elevation and a blank record. Divide the note into completed scope, excluded elevations, unresolved conditions and specialist referrals. Write one refusal letter to a fictitious client who asks for an unsupported certificate. Use photographs, drawn plans, fictitious work orders and inert desk materials only. The trainer checks accuracy and stops any proposal to carry out unauthorised real-world work.

procedure: Compare the work order with what was actually cleaned, inspected or seen, and note the viewpoint for each observation.
Record each observation with its location, viewpoint, time and photograph reference where permitted.
List each excluded elevation and the reason it is excluded.
List each unresolved condition, with the named referral, the person notified and the time.
Remove any competence, safety or compliance wording that the evidence does not support.
Check any extra scope request against the written quote, and obtain written agreement before any added work.
Issue the restricted handover to the site controller or client, keep a copy, and record the date sent.
Decline any request for an unsupported certificate in writing, with the reason and the recommended referral.

workedExamples.situation: A client asks for a signed statement that all high-level glazing is safe, after a visual clean from the ground.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first safe action, and what do you write?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not sign the statement. Decline in writing, giving the reason: the high-level glazing was not reached or authorised, so the evidence does not support a safety claim. Write the restricted handover that lists the ground-level scope as completed, the high-level glazing as excluded, and a recommended specialist assessment with the referral named. Record the request, the decline and the time, and send the handover to the site controller.

workedExamples.situation: A client refuses to pay the full quote because the upper-floor windows were not cleaned, although the quote excluded them in writing.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Who decides on the payment, and what do you put on the record?
workedExamples.reasoning: The payment is not yours to decide. Show the written scope and the exclusion, and refer the dispute to the business owner or supervisor. Do not promise a discount or a credit. Record the client's objection, the written exclusion, the referral and the time. Under the consumer rules, the accepted quote sets the scope, and any change to it needs agreement.

workedExamples.situation: On the day, the owner asks you to add the upper windows to the job because the ladder is already on site and the weather is fine.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must happen before any upper window is cleaned?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not start the upper windows. Work above ground level needs written employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and any required licence, and the ladder on site is not an authorisation. Under the state or territory consumer rules, extra work needs the customer's permission before it is done. Record the request, refer it to the supervisor, and record the upper windows as excluded in the handover until a written scope is agreed.

equipmentAndPpe: Restricted handover template with four sections: completed scope, excluded elevations, unresolved conditions and referrals.
Observation record with viewpoint, time and photograph reference fields.
Referral list for building specialists, electricians and the site controller (desk materials only).
Fictitious quote and scope sheet for the tabletop exercise.
Decline letter template for requests for unsupported certificates.
For any future real site, PPE and access equipment are set by the site controller and the risk assessment. None is used in this desk-based lesson.

commonErrors.error: Writing that all windows are certified or safe after ground-level observation only.
commonErrors.prevention: Decline in writing, and list the excluded elevations and their reason.

commonErrors.error: Leaving excluded elevations out of the handover.
commonErrors.prevention: List every excluded elevation with its reason, so that the client can see what was not inspected.

commonErrors.error: Agreeing extra work verbally and doing it before the agreement is written.
commonErrors.prevention: Obtain written agreement before any added work, and record it.

commonErrors.error: Mixing observed conditions with the cleaner's conclusions.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep observations, inferences and approvals in separate entries.

commonErrors.error: Writing a handover that has no named referral or time.
commonErrors.prevention: Name the referral, the person notified and the time for each unresolved condition.

commonErrors.error: Treating the handover as a certificate of building safety.
commonErrors.prevention: State the handover's limits, and say that it is not a certificate.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Consumer claims. The ACCC states that claims must be accurate and backed by reasonable grounds, that a statement can breach the rules by creating a false impression even when each word is true, that silence can mislead, and that intention does not matter (ACCC, false or misleading claims; page metadata 28 June 2026).

Quotes and extra work. Western Australia's consumer guidance says an accepted quote is binding, that the tradesperson must get permission before extra work, and that work done without permission need not be paid for (page last updated 4 September 2026). The Northern Territory's guidance says an accepted quote binds both parties and that extra work outside the quote is not payable unless approved beforehand (no date shown).

Licence and height notice. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems, and it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. The licence thresholds for boom-type platforms are set out in the instruction above. Check the rule in your state or territory and obtain written employer authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule. Stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

Electrical notice. This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing and altering an installation.

qualityStandard: The handover separates completed scope, excluded elevations, unresolved conditions and specialist referrals.
No competence, safety or compliance claim is made that the evidence does not show.
A request for an unsupported certificate is declined in writing, with the reason recorded.
Unresolved conditions and named referrals are recorded with the person notified and the time.
Any extra scope is recorded as agreed in writing before it is done.
documentationEvidence: Restricted handover with the four sections and the limits statement.
Observation record with viewpoint, time and photograph reference.
Written decline for any request for an unsupported certificate.
Scope change record showing the written agreement, or the refusal, for any extra work.
summary: The handover is restricted to what was observed and authorised, with completed scope, excluded elevations and referrals kept apart.
No safety, competence or compliance statement is given where the evidence does not support it, and an all-windows-certified-safe request is declined in writing.
Named referrals and unresolved conditions are recorded, so the client can see what was not inspected.

knowledgeChecks.question: For inspection evidence and restricted handover, what evidence must be established before allocating work, and which facts are still unverified?
options: An 'all windows certified safe' statement issued after ground-level observation of the building by the crew at the front
A verbal summary to the client without a record of the visit at all, the findings, the photos and the time
Records of only the work completed, with no unresolved conditions listed in the handover or the final report
Observed and authorised work recorded, unresolved conditions and named referrals listed, and no safety certification claimed

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks for a signed statement that all glazing is safe, after ground-level observation only. What is correct?
options: Sign it to keep the client satisfied with the work, the price, the finish and the total on the day
Decline in writing, state what was observed and its limits, and recommend specialist assessment
Sign it with a note that the upper floors were not seen by the crew or the owner at the visit

knowledgeChecks.question: Extra work outside the agreed quote is requested on site. What must happen?
options: Start it and bill for it afterwards, once the client has been told
Obtain the client's agreement before doing it, and record that agreement
Do it if the site controller says so verbally on the day of the job
